issue: Release U-Boot bootcmd=run ramboot suggests uEnv.txt is not imported (BOOT-007; MiaUI reports the same), but RetroArch alpha 0.1 can only find its root filesystem through uEnv.txt's root=/dev/mmcblk0p2 (no ramdisk, no root= in DTB or kernel).
status: Resolved offline (PR #5) in favour of uEnv.txt being applied: check_boot_flag replaces bootcmd=run ramboot with run mmcboot after the environment is loaded, and mmcboot imports uEnv.txt before fatloading the images (BOOT-015, BOOT-016). Executing the handoff on Koriki v1.0 puts its uEnv.txt init=/init into /chosen bootargs. Alpha 0.1's root= is applied the same way. The MiaUI statement and the original BOOT-007 reading are refuted statically.
next_validation: P-UENV on the V3 capture remains the hardware confirmation: the offline prediction is outcome uenv-applied (init=/init present in /proc/cmdline on Koriki).

issue: Earlier reports call Koriki 1.0.3.1 a "stock-like kernel" and GarlicOS a "closed stock-derived binary". Stock kernels are flower@flower-B85M-D2V builds with Linaro GCC 4.7.3 and a different configuration (umonitor/xHCI present, EHCI/Bluetooth/fbcon absent); Koriki kernels are ctalon@endymion GCC 4.9.4 builds that share 119 vendor-only functions with stock but are not the stock build. The GarlicOS kernel is a separate blackseraph build from essentially the stock tree with the stock toolchain.
status: Resolved in part: "stock-like" holds for vendor BSP code, not for build, configuration or USB stack. Test-plan wording should say "vendor-BSP-derived".
next_validation: None needed statically; a runtime capture should record which kernel build actually booted (uname -v).

issue: The Actions 2015 Form 20-F lists ATM7039S with 32-bit DDR (ID-001), but every stock RG35XX loader configures bus_width_selector=1, printed as x16, with 256 MiB and one chip select, and sets DXGCR bit 0 only on byte lanes 2 and 3 in some paths. The pinned U-Boot source falls back to 496 MiB when the AFI size is invalid (MEM-003).
status: Unresolved. Most likely the SoC supports 32-bit DRAM while this board populates a 16-bit interface, but that is board inference, not evidence. Whether lanes 2/3 are disabled at run time depends on which conditional path executes.
next_validation: Board photograph of the DRAM package(s) and part number; or a read-only serial boot log showing the "DRAM init ... x%dbus ... Ok:DCU_CFG" lines. No register access.

issue: MEM-005 reads the bootloader.ini record at +0x1c (256 MiB, 1 chip select, rcc 0x48) as the DRAM configuration. MEM-006 shows that on cold boot the ini word at +0x2c selects the record at +0x4c (cs 0, rcc 0, capacity 0), so chip selects, row/column codes and capacity are detected, and the +0x1c record is what the success path writes back.
status: Resolved statically for the cold-boot path in favour of MEM-006. MEM-005's copy routine and field offsets remain correct; its 'configured 256 MiB' is an expected detection result, not an input. The shipped +0x1c values match the write-back only under the single-rank x16 2 Gb hypothesis.
next_validation: A read-only serial log of a normal boot (no register access). For 20231014 the reconstruction predicts, in order: "DRAM init mode0,type16,2cs,x16bus,rcc0x0,wrodt2,rdodt2,drv9,468MHz.@180525_R...", a "Fail:..." lane-status line, the same line with 1cs, then "Ok:DCU_CFG:0x202c,256MByte Cap."; older releases print wrodt1,rdodt1,drvc. A different sequence falsifies the training or probe hypotheses, not the formulas.

issue: The stock dossier (PR #3) said app.bin loads and checksums U-Boot. Instruction-level tracing shows bootloader.bin loads U-Boot (0xb4065bf0) before app.bin runs, and no loader stage checks the uImage magic or CRC; app.bin only gates on a chip identity, writes back bootloader.ini when the SFVD record is missing, and jumps to the entry bootloader.bin passed in r0.
status: Resolved statically in favour of BOOT-013/BOOT-014. app.bin does contain an SD driver and an unreferenced "load uboot" string, which explains the earlier reading.
next_validation: A serial log of a normal boot prints "load uboot: load address is 0x5000000, entry point is 0x5000040" before "in fourth" (app.bin) if the order is right.

issue: Loader block 0 maps CMU_DEVCLKEN0 (0xb01600a0) bit 4 to boot code 0, which the loader turns into AFI boot_dev 0x20 (sd0) and the SD read paths; the mainline S500 clock driver names bit 4 the NAND gate and bit 5 the SD0 gate.
status: Resolved by inference (PR #8). The observed boot took block-0 code 2, which block 0 selects when CMU_DEVCLKEN0 bit 7 is set; under the mainline S500 names bit 7 is the SD2 gate, consistent with a ROM that booted from SD2 and left SD2's clock on. The bit-4 -> code 0 branch (mainline: NAND gate) is the one this unit did not take, so the earlier conflict came from assuming TF1 = SD0. Not read from hardware.
next_validation: None required. A register read is not authorized; an early serial log or vendor documentation would confirm.

issue: PR #3 described loader 0x3800-0x4c00 as a 5 KiB high-entropy per-release area (possibly encrypted or signed). PR #5 places it inside bootloader.ini, shows no traced code reads it on the SD path, and shows app.bin writes the whole 20-sector ini back from SRAM.
status: Reinterpreted, not proven: best explained as uninitialised SRAM captured by the write-back on each master card. Nothing suggests a signature.
next_validation: Offline: obtain a second dump of a stock card after a factory first boot (if one exists publicly) and compare; on hardware this would require reading the card before and after a boot, which is not authorized.

issue: PR #4 (MEM-006, ddr_model.capacity_probe) treated a row probe without an alias as the error 0xf000fa11. The instructions 0xb4068cec..0xb4068dd0 end the row search at an alias or at exponent 31 and otherwise leave the row code at 0, reporting 13 rows; the exponent-32 check that would return 0xf000fa11 can never fire.
status: Resolved by instruction reading and emulation; ddr_model corrected (48 geometries, 0 mismatches). PR #4's committed evidence covered only aliasing geometries and is unaffected.
next_validation: None needed offline.

issue: PR #4 listed 0x2a00fa11, 0x9a00fa11, 0xdf00fa11, 0xf000fa11 and 0xc000fa11 as values the DRAM routine returns. 0xb4068f34..0xb4068f50 prints each as 'Fail: 0x...' and returns 0x1747fa11 instead; only 0x1017fa11 is returned unchanged.
status: Resolved by instruction reading and scenario emulation.
next_validation: None needed offline.

issue: PR #4 (MEM-006) said the parameter write-back 0xb4066280 runs on success. The caller joins the success and the 'ddr init error' paths at 0xb4066744, so the write-back and the AFI write also run after a failed init, with the forced 2048 MiB capacity.
status: Resolved: both writes happen, but main then takes the ADFU exit, so neither reaches U-Boot or the card.
next_validation: None needed offline.

issue: PR #4 listed 0xb4069254 as the pre-DRAM clock setup; PR #5 called it a PMIC status read. It is an ADFU-entry check (PMIC reg 0x35 bit 1; GPIO 0x55aa55aa handshake on non-SD0 boot codes) with no DDR effect.
status: Resolved by instruction reading and emulation (adfu-request scenario).
next_validation: None needed offline.

issue: The resume init issues PIR 0x3f, whose bit 5 is DRAMRST (RESET# pulse) in the related RK3288 PUBL layout, while every other feature of mode 1 (no DRAMINIT, PREA/REF bursts, no probe or memory test, a jump to a kernel resume vector, reads of kernel-left data at DRAM 0x400) presumes DRAM contents survive self-refresh. A DDR3 RESET# pulse would void that. Mode 1 also shortens tDINIT2 to about 100 ns and sends 0x3f for LPDDR types, which have no RESET#.
status: Open. Not decidable offline without the PUBL v1 databook or a public driver for this PUBL revision with a resume path.
next_validation: Offline: a PUBL v1 databook or a vendor (e.g. older Rockchip RK30/RK3188) DDR driver with a self-refresh resume sequence. Hardware: a suspend/resume cycle with a read-only UART log (separate approval required).

issue: Which MMC controller holds the TF1 boot card. U-Boot loads uImage, ramdisk.img and kernel.dtb with fatload mmc 0:1, and BOOT-016 reads mmc 0 as SD0 at 0xb0230000 (registration order SD0, SD2). Koriki's Linux scripts place the boot card (mmcblk0, emmc_boot_card) on b0238000 (SD2) and TF2 (sd_card) on b0230000, which also carries card-detect GPIO and the share_uart pin state.
status: Resolved offline for Koriki v1.0 (PR #8), building on OBS-001: the TF1 boot card is on SD2. The executed chain block-0 code 2 -> AFI 0x22 -> emmcboot (devpart 1:1) -> U-Boot mmc 1 = SD2 0xb0238000 -> boot_dev=sd2 is the only one of six emulated hypotheses that reproduces the observed command line (BOOT-022). U-Boot numbering is registration order and does not shift when SD0 is empty (BOOT-023); Linux numbering is chosen independently from boot_dev (STOR-003). BOOT-016 described the AFI 0x20 path, which this unit did not take. ROM behaviour, the CMU bit and the AFI bytes remain inferred, not observed.
next_validation: Optional confirmation, not needed to use the result: an early serial log would show "bootdev= 0x22", "emmc boot" and U-Boot's mmc messages; /proc/bootdev (read-only) would show the kernel's g_boot_dev. A capture with a second card in TF2 would show sd_card on b0230000.

issue: The DRAM and loader reconstruction (PR #4-#6) modelled the code-0 (SD0) path. On the observed code-2 path the pre-DRAM routine 0xb4069254 also performs the GPIO 0x55aa55aa ADFU handshake that is skipped for code 0 (BOOT-021), and app.bin/bootloader.bin branches keyed on the boot code were exercised only for code 0 in the committed DRAM evidence.
status: Open. The storage reads and AFI are identical for codes 0 and 2 (boot_chain.py boot-path), but the DRAM-stage emulation (dram_complete.py) has not been re-run with boot code 2, so code-dependent DRAM-stage behaviour is not yet reconstructed for the path the device actually takes.
next_validation: Offline: re-run the DRAM-stage scenarios with boot code 2 and diff the MMIO sequences against code 0.
